n8.starta-servern-och-las.1: Start the server and read the log
n8.starta-servern-och-las.2: Among the startup logs there are three lines that sum up module 6:
n8.starta-servern-och-las.3: The numbers are a worked example for a GPU with 80 GB. Your values depend on GPU, model, version and flags.
n8.starta-servern-och-las.4: Available KV cache memory: what was left after weights, activations and overhead. That whole area is turned into blocks.
n8.starta-servern-och-las.5: GPU KV cache size: the same area in tokens. Here 47.5 GiB ÷ 128 KiB per token.
n8.starta-servern-och-las.6: Maximum concurrency: the pool divided by max-model-len. That many sequences fit if they are all at maximum length. If they are shorter, more fit.
n8.starta-servern-och-las.7: Then send a request. The API follows the OpenAI format:
n8.starta-servern-och-las.8: If the log says max-model-len does not fit in the KV cache: lower max-model-len, raise gpu-memory-utilization or quantize.
n8.mat-med-metrics.2: The server exposes Prometheus metrics on /metrics. The most important ones map directly to the concepts in the course.
n8.mat-med-metrics.22: Requests in the batch right now
n8.mat-med-metrics.28: Share of the KV pool in use (1 = full)
n8.mat-med-metrics.39: Metric names have changed between versions. Check them against the documentation for the version you run.
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.5: Server won’t start: max-model-len doesn’t fit
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.6: The KV pool can’t hold a single sequence of the max length
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.7: Lower --max-model-len, quantize, fp8 KV cache or more GPUs
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.9: More requests than the batch size or the KV pool can hold
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.10: More replicas, shorter context, raise --max-num-seqs if KV memory allows
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.11: High TTFT despite an empty queue
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.12: Long prompts are prefilled from scratch every time
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.13: Put the shared part first in the prompt so the prefix cache hits
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.15: Something varies early in the prompt, such as the time or a username
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.16: Move the varying part to the end
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.17: ITL rises as more clients connect
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.18: Bigger batch, more KV to read per step
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.20: ITL stutters when long prompts arrive
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.21: Prefill takes too big a share of the step
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.24: The KV pool fills up while running
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.25: Lower --max-num-seqs, fp8 KV cache, more memory
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.26: Low throughput, the GPU looks idle
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.27: Too few sequences per step: decode is memory-bound
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.28: More concurrent load per GPU, speculative decoding
n8.felsokning-symptom-och.30: max_tokens or max-model-len reached, often because of a long reasoning chain
n8.starta-servern-och-las.n9: Every number in the course is computed for Llama-3-8B. The server above starts Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: the same shapes and the same number of layers, but 3.1 uses RoPE scaling and a 128,000-token context, which module 7 covers.
n8.disaggregerad-prefill-och-decode.2: Prefill and decode have different bottlenecks: prefill is compute-bound (once the prompt is large enough), decode is memory-bound. Running both on the same GPUs lets a long prompt disturb everyone waiting for the next token — ITL spikes exactly when a new request arrives.
n8.disaggregerad-prefill-och-decode.3: Disaggregation splits them: some GPUs only run prefill, others only decode, and the KV cache is moved between them. The decode pool then keeps a steady rate, whatever the prompts look like.
n8.disaggregerad-prefill-och-decode.4:
KV per request = T · 32 layers · 8 heads · 128 · 2 (K and V) · 2 bytes
Llama-3-8B, T = 5,000   → 625 MiB
100 Gbit/s              → ~52 ms
n8.disaggregerad-prefill-och-decode.5: The transfer costs time and bandwidth. It pays off only with a fast interconnect (NVLink or RDMA) and when ITL requirements are strict. In vLLM it is enabled with --kv-transfer-config; it is a feature for large installations, not for a single GPU.
n8.disaggregerad-prefill-och-decode.6: What you gain and what you pay:
n8.disaggregerad-prefill-och-decode.15: steady ITL, independent of prompt length
n8.disaggregerad-prefill-och-decode.19: The hand-over costs too: a request waits for the whole KV cache to arrive before decoding starts. A long context on a slow link eats the gain.
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.1: Multi-LoRA: many models on one GPU
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.2: A LoRA adapter is two small matrices per weight: B [d, r] and A [r, d] with rank r, typically 8–64. The base model stays untouched and is shared by all adapters.
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.3:
y = x W + (α/r) · x A B
Base model 8B in bf16   16 GB (shared)
Adapter r = 16         ~84 MB
32 adapters            ~2.7 GB
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.4: vLLM serves many adapters against the same base model at once. Requests with different adapters land in the same batch and the kernels apply the right adapter per request — so one GPU can serve many customers who each have their own fine-tuned variant.
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.5: The price is a little extra work per token when many adapters are mixed in one batch, and that quality never exceeds the base model. The adapter changes behaviour and style, not knowledge.
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.7: Each request names its adapter in the model field (for example "code"). The server keeps only --max-loras adapters active at a time and loads more on demand.
n8.multi-lora-manga-modeller-pa.8: The adapter is added to the frozen weight; no shapes change, so an adapter can be moved between machines and merged into the base model if you want a single file.
